examples.note: Bare family call defaults to live-DOM run.

allow_anchor_dock.description: Override for the Anchor-Dock root guard: a bare root_handle raw dump whose resolved root is an Anchor Dock (global or local) is refused with a peek/render teaching error unless this is true.

ancestor_notes.description: Ancestor notes are suppressed on chronological renders: when sort_by is 'created' or 'modified' (either direction), or recent is any selection -- a date window ('1w'), 'curated', or an item-count 'last N'/'newest N'/'bottom N' -- every non-leaf of the final render forest (the root included when it is a non-leaf) renders HEADING-ONLY and leaf notes print -- membership and ordering are untouched. An item-count recent selection alone still keeps document-order excerpts unless you also pass a sort. Renders with no sort and no recent selection keep ancestor notes -- except LENS renders (slice_group.render / sift / merge.render, or any render_lens selection), where the connective scaffolding above the lens's input roots (the LCA down to each input root) renders heading-only by default EVEN IN DOCUMENT order; the input roots and their subtrees are unaffected. Pass ancestor_notes: true to include ancestor notes on a chronological render and to restore the lens scaffold notes (the sole opt-out; default false).

descend_policy.description: Boundary leg of the traversal pair (with recursive, the depth leg). 'all' (the default) descends into child Anchor Docks; 'stop_at_child_anchors' stops the walk at them -- the boundary node itself still matches and renders as a leaf signpost. 'stop_at_child_docks' is an accepted alias; the canonical wire spelling is stop_at_child_anchors. Under the depth cap (recursive=False) the boundary is moot: the cap stops the descent first.

full_uuids.description: Print FULL 36-char UUIDs in headings-only [id] tokens instead of the short 8-hex handles (the default: short, lengthened just enough to be unique when the 8-hex prefix is ambiguous in the cache). JSON/structured outputs always carry full UUIDs regardless.

group_handle.description: Persisted slice-group id/prefix, full name, or semantic short name (final pipe-delimited segment, trailing [n] index stripped; case-insensitive).

headings_only.description: Titles/UUIDs plus dock.peek's four-field end-of-line metrics (▸N direct children · desc:N descendants · self:title+note size · tree:self+all descendants) from the operation cache, completed/suppressed/out-of-slice descendants included (not the visible child count). Lines whose note carries Cartographer/beacon source-map markers (mapped source code) carry none of it. ▸0 = known leaf; ▸? = node/count unavailable. Counts are snapshot metadata, not live verification or permission to complete/delete a subtree. The [id] token on each heading prints the node's SHORT resolver-compatible handle (8 hex; lengthened just enough to be unique when the 8-hex prefix is ambiguous in the cache) — pass full_uuids: true for full UUIDs.

include_archives.description: Default false. true adds the active export archives to this read: archived subtrees appear under the parent they were exported from, each archived node marked 📦, read-only. The exported subtree's parent must stay in Workflowy (it may be moved, but it must stay under the root you search or sift from); every other rule applies exactly as if nothing had been exported. A handle that misses live Workflowy is answered from the archives automatically, with or without this flag. Cannot combine with output_file or push_to_modal. Rules: system(verb='describe', params={'of': 'archives.list', 'detail': 'full'}).

match_scope.description: WHERE a semantic tag search reads tags. 'name' (the default for tag-search surfaces: slice/group renders, lightning_rod render_tags/gather) matches only the trailing tag region of the node NAME, read by the core splitter -- a '#tag' mentioned mid-title as prose, or living only in a note body, does NOT match. 'name_and_note' matches a tag anywhere in the name or note (Workflowy-search parity) and is the default for free-text search (lightning_rod render_search; the sift query half). Suppression and the family postfixes (--expand/--suppress/--deprecated) follow this scope: under 'name' they count only in the trailing tag region of the name; the global never-expand tag (e.g. #wfy-suppress) counts only in the trailing tag region under EVERY scope.

output_file.description: Write the render output to this file; a compact file-write summary is returned instead of the content. Resolved on the daemon's own host: on a Windows daemon '/mnt/<drive>/…' maps to '<DRIVE>:\…' and any other POSIX-absolute path is refused with a teaching error; on a WSL daemon 'X:\…' maps to '/mnt/<drive>/…'; relative paths are refused everywhere. The result's path_record echoes requested/resolved/translated/host.

recent.description: Most-recent selection token. A SELECTION -- it never reorders; presentation order stays with sort_by/sort_direction. Count: 'last N' or 'newest N' select the N NEWEST leaves by recent_by (the sort_by axis when it is a timestamp, else 'modified') -- whatever the sort direction. 'bottom N' instead keeps the POSITIONAL tail of the current render order (the legacy 'last N' behavior; an old wire blob without a selection field means this). Time window: '1w', '3d', '12h' (measured back from the newest item in scope, not the clock). 'curated' (slice-group scope only): everything newer than the most recently CREATED already-tagged node -- the untagged material awaiting curation. sort_direction only orders the selected set (asc = oldest first) and never changes which items were chosen.

recent_by.description: Recency basis for an item-count recent selection ('last N' / 'newest N'): 'created' | 'modified'. Omitted: the sort_by axis when it is a timestamp, else 'modified'. Inert for time windows, 'curated' and 'bottom N'.

recursive.description: Depth leg of the traversal pair (with descend_policy, the boundary leg). True (default) = the ordinary unbounded walk. False = the scope root's own heading and note plus each DIRECT child's heading and note, and nothing deeper -- child Docks and plain nodes alike; descend_policy is then moot. A RAW-ROOT traversal policy: honoured on the bare-root surfaces (glimpse.run root_handle, anchor.dock.render, the estate {dock} form); a slice-group, lens or Lightning Rod selection refuses it loudly -- its membership is defined over the whole scope, so a depth cap would silently change it.

render_spec.description: Literal 'modal', one simple form (group name, {group}, {dock}, {node}, {subtree}, {tags,root}, {symbols,root}, the long {ref,kind} alias, bare Dock handle), or a full render-spec object/JSON string; short-circuits explicit scope fields. One PARCEL renders here; an estate of several parcels uses estate, not run.

repository_view.description: Clean Markdown commit view for a beacon slice: the render becomes exactly what you could commit to a source repository, with every Workflowy trace removed. Files render as paths relative to their repository, sorted by path; each tagged function, class, region or Markdown section renders in source order as 'kind `signature`' with its labels and its beacon comment (headings_only mode) or, in the full mode, plus the slurped docstring and comments as fenced blocks. No node handle, no absolute path, no metric, no emoji marker, no #tag syntax, no Anchor Point reference, and no plain Workflowy node that the tag family happened to reach (the count is reported in the reply as a '> Repository view:' line above the document, or the repository_view key with output_file -- never inside the document). Screen and output_file carry the same bytes. The document order is fixed (file paths, then source position), so a committed slice changes only when a tagged function's signature, comment or labels change; sort_by created/modified and recent are refused rather than ignored, as are as_markdown: false, full_uuids, push_to_modal, include_archives, a live-DOM or modal glimpse.run, and non-slice search tiers.

root_handle.description: Raw-dump scope alone; slice-group override root with group_handle.

sort_by.description: Presentation sort axis: 'created' | 'modified'; 'none' forces document order. Omitted on a group scope: the slice group's saved default sort is inherited. A timestamp sort_by is also the default recency basis for an item-count 'newest' selection when recent_by is omitted.

sort_direction.description: Presentation order only: 'asc' (default) = oldest first, 'desc' = newest first. It NEVER changes which items a recency selection (recent) chose -- selection and order are independent. Requires an explicit timestamp sort_by ('created'|'modified'): a direction with no sort basis is refused loudly (sort_direction_without_sort_by) -- even when a slice group's saved default sort would supply one (the guard checks the raw call params; pass sort_by explicitly). A recency selection never needs it.

returns.description: Successful results preserve the established GLIMPSE-family contract: raw Markdown/text strings, structured full/UUID results, modal acknowledgements, or artifact summaries. Scope truth table: neither group_handle nor root_handle = live DOM; root_handle only = raw dump; group_handle only = persisted slice group at its saved root; both = the group lens at an override root. render_spec='modal' reads and exactly re-projects the dock, including frozen DOM captures; a render-spec object is the paste fallback. push_to_modal writes a server-side scope into the dock, the dual of modal readback: honored for explicit scopes AND for a render_spec blob (routed through the same push funnel; the blob's focus is dropped), invalid for a bare live-DOM call, and refused with an actionable error for render_spec='modal' (cross-tab read-then-push copy is a pending feature). recent (most-recent selection; legacy tail/since accepted) takes 'last N' | 'newest N' (the N NEWEST leaves by recent_by -- the sort_by axis when it is a timestamp, else 'modified' -- whatever the direction), 'bottom N' (the positional tail of the current order), a window like '1w' (measured back from the newest item in scope, not the clock), or 'curated' (requires group_handle and pivots on creation time). sort_direction only orders the selected set (asc = oldest first) and never changes which items were chosen. match_scope selects WHERE a tag search reads tags and applies only to a slice-group scope: 'name' (default) = the trailing tag region of the node name, 'name_and_note' = tags anywhere in name or note. Suppression and postfixes follow the same scope (under 'name' they count only in the trailing tag region; the global never-expand tag is trailing-only under every scope). Omitted sort_by inherits a slice group's saved default; 'none' forces document order. headings_only=true in Markdown mode is the compact UUID harvest. Low-level descend_policy='stop_at_child_anchors' means stop at child Anchor Docks. recursive (default true) is the depth leg of the traversal pair: false on a bare root_handle raw dump renders that root's own heading and note plus each DIRECT child's heading and note, and nothing deeper (child Docks and plain nodes alike; descend_policy is then moot); it is refused loudly for a group_handle scope or a live-DOM render. ancestor_notes (default false) is the U6 teaching flag: chronological renders -- sort_by created/modified in either direction, or ANY recent selection (a date window, 'curated', or an item-count 'last N'/'newest N'/'bottom N') -- suppress ancestor notes automatically (every non-leaf of the final render forest, the root included, renders heading-only; leaf notes print); pass ancestor_notes=true to include them. Renders with no sort and no recent selection always keep ancestor notes -- except a render_lens projection (a render_spec blob carrying lightning mode render_lens), where the connective scaffolding above the lens's input roots renders heading-only by default even in document order and ancestor_notes=true restores it. A legitimately empty result is delivered as the literal string '(empty)', never a bare blank string (the public funnel's empty-output stub).

operation_doc.summary: Render the live DOM, the docked modal's current view, a known root, or a slice-group scope. Truth table: root_handle alone = raw subtree dump; group_handle alone = curated slice; both = that lens at an override root; neither = live DOM. render_spec='modal' re-projects what the dock shows with no UUIDs. A raw dump rooted AT an Anchor Dock is refused (anchor.dock.peek/render, or allow_anchor_dock=true). A render specification is exactly one entry of an estate; see estate. render_spec also accepts a group name/{group}, {dock}, {node}, {subtree}, {tags,root}, {symbols,root}, the long {ref,kind} alias, or a bare Dock handle ({node} renders that node alone with its note; {subtree} every descendant; see estate for the per-kind default reads). Read slice groups (and also lenses) through the same funnel; 'modal' remains the readback token.
